questions.stem: Ocean currents in the Northern Hemisphere tend to deflect to the right, while those in the Southern Hemisphere deflect to the left. What is the primary cause of this deflection?

options.option_text: The Coriolis Effect caused by the Earth's rotation
The gravitational pull of the Moon on the oceans
The uneven heating of the Earth's surface by the Sun
The magnetic field generated by the Earth's core

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Coriolis Effect is an inertial force resulting from the Earth's rotation on its axis. Because the Earth is a spinning sphere, points at the equator move much faster than points near the poles. This causes moving fluids (like massive ocean currents and wind systems) to deflect to the RIGHT in the Northern Hemisphere and to the LEFT in the Southern Hemisphere.
DECOY BUSTING: The Moon's gravity causes Tides. Uneven solar heating causes the creation of winds and ocean currents in the first place, but the Coriolis effect dictates their DIRECTION of curve. The magnetic field protects us from solar wind.
EXAM INSIGHT: Because of the Coriolis effect, hurricanes and typhoons spin counter-clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere, but clockwise in the Southern Hemisphere.
